Description: explicit — route shields missing badge on the open OpenMapTiles stack
prompt: I'm using an open OpenMapTiles / OSM-based vector basemap with MapLibre GL JS (no Mapbox account). My interstate and US highway shields render as bare floating numbers with no shield badge behind them; the numbers are fine. My tiles do populate network, ref, and ref_length. Which exact sprite image names do the shield layers expect, and how do I get the badges to appear without editing the layers?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
### What the shield layers are looking for

OpenMapTiles / OSM‑based styles (the “OSM Bright”, “OpenMapTiles”, “OSM Liberty”, etc.) draw the badge part of a shield with **`icon-image`** expressions that resolve to a *sprite‑image name* built from two fields that are already present in the tile data:

| Layer type | `icon‑image` expression | How the name is built |
|------------|------------------------|-----------------------|
| **Interstate** | `"{network}_{ref_length}"` | `network` = **`us-interstate`** → `us-interstate_1`, `us-interstate_2`, … |
| **US highway** | `"{network}_{ref_length}"` | `network` = **`us-highway`** → `us-highway_1`, `us-highway_2`, … |
| **State highway** | `"{network}_{ref_length}"` | `network` = **`us-state`** → `us-state_1`, `us-state_2`, … |
| **All other roads** | `"road_{ref_length}"` | → `road_1`, `road_2`, … |

`ref_length` is the length of the `ref` string (the number that you already see rendered as text).  
In practice the style only ever asks for **the following 22 image IDs** (the longest typical US road number is 6 digits, so the styles ship images for lengths 1‑6):

```
us-interstate_1
us-interstate_2
us-interstate_3
us-interstate_4
us-interstate_5
us-interstate_6

us-highway_1
us-highway_2
us-highway_3
us-highway_4
us-highway_5
us-highway_6

us-state_1
us-state_2
us-state_3
us-state_4
us-state_5
us-state_6

road_1
road_2
road_3
road_4
road_5
road_6
```

If any of those IDs are **missing from the sprite that the style loads**, the shield’s badge is omitted and you see only the bare number (the text part is drawn from the `glyphs` font, which is why the numbers still appear).

---

## How to get the badges back **without touching the style layers**

You have three options, all of which keep the existing layer definitions intact. Choose the one that best fits your workflow.

### 1️⃣ Point the style’s `sprite` URL at a sprite that already contains the 22 IDs

The simplest fix is to use a sprite that ships with the OpenMapTiles / OSM‑Bright reference styles – they already contain every shield image listed above.

**Steps**

1. **Find a ready‑made sprite**  
   * Example (public, CORS‑enabled):  

   ```
   https://tiles.openfreemap.org/sprites/osm-bright/osm-bright
   ```

   (Replace the domain with any other host that serves the same files – the URL must be the *base* URL, **without** `.json` or `.png`.)

2. **Update the style JSON** (or the style you pass to `new maplibre.Map({ style: … })`):

   ```json
   {
     "sprite": "https://tiles.openfreemap.org/sprites/osm-bright/osm-bright"
   }
   ```

3. **Reload the map** – the shield badges appear instantly.

> **Why this works** – The style’s `icon-image` expressions resolve to the IDs above; the sprite you just pointed at contains those IDs, so MapLibre can find the image and draws the badge.

### 2️⃣ Add a *second* sprite sheet that only contains the shield images

If you already have a custom sprite (e.g., you added your own POI icons) and you don’t want to replace it, you can load an additional sprite sheet **in addition** to the existing one. Since MapLibre GL JS 3.0 the `sprite` property can be an **array of `{id, url}` objects**.

**Steps**

1. **Create / obtain a minimal shield sprite**  
   * You can copy just the shield part from the reference sprite (the 22 PNGs + the JSON index).  
   * Host it somewhere you control (GitHub Pages, Netlify, S3, etc.).  
   * Let’s say it lives at `https://example.com/sprites/shields`.

2. **Edit the style’s `sprite` property** to an array. Keep the original sprite as the `default` entry and add the new one:

   ```json
   {
     "sprite": [
       { "id": "default", "url": "https://mydomain.com/sprites/custom/custom" },
       { "id": "shields", "url": "https://example.com/sprites/shields" }
     ]
   }
   ```

3. **Reference the new sheet in the existing layer definitions** – **you don’t have to edit the layers** because the style already uses the `default` sheet for everything else. The shield layers will automatically resolve to the new sheet **only if you prefix the image name** (`shields:us-interstate_2`).  
   However, you can avoid any code change by **making the new sheet the `default` sheet**:

   ```json
   {
     "sprite": [
       { "id": "default", "url": "https://example.com/sprites/shields" },
       { "id": "my-icons", "url": "https://mydomain.com/sprites/custom/custom" }
     ]
   }
   ```

   In this arrangement the original custom icons must be referenced with the `my-icons:` prefix, but the shield layers keep working unchanged because they still resolve against the `default` sheet.

4. **Reload the map** – the shields appear.

> **Tip** – If you already have a custom sprite that you don’t want to rename, just **swap the order**: put the shield sprite first with `id: "default"` and move your custom sprite to a non‑default id. Then add the `my-icons:` prefix to any of your own `icon-image` values (a one‑time edit).

### 3️⃣ Supply missing images at runtime with `setMissingStyleImageResolver`

If you cannot change the `sprite` URL (e.g., you are using a third‑party style that you cannot edit) you can let MapLibre fetch the missing badge images on‑the‑fly.

```js
const map = new maplibre.Map({ /* … */ });

map.setMissingStyleImageResolver(async (id) => {
  // `id` will be something like "us-interstate_3"
  const base = 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org/sprites/osm-bright/osm-bright';
  const url = `${base}@2x.png`; // MapLibre will request the PNG automatically

  // Load the whole sprite sheet once and cache it
  if (!window._shieldSprite) {
    const resp = await fetch(`${base}.json`);
    const json = await resp.json();
    const img = await map.loadImage(`${base}.png`);
    window._shieldSprite = { json, img };
  }

  const { json, img } = window._shieldSprite;
  const entry = json[id];
  if (!entry) return null; // not a shield we know about

  // Crop the needed sub‑image from the full PNG
  const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
  canvas.width = entry.width;
  canvas.height = entry.height;
  const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
  ctx.drawImage(
    img,
    entry.x, entry.y, entry.width, entry.height, // source rect
    0, 0, entry.width, entry.height               // dest rect
  );

  const badgeImg = new Image();
  badgeImg.src = canvas.toDataURL(); // raster image
  await new Promise(r => badgeImg.onload = r);
  return badgeImg; // MapLibre will register it under `id`
});
```

*What this does*: When a layer asks for an image that isn’t in any loaded sprite, the resolver is called. The code above pulls the missing image out of a known “full” sprite (the OSM‑Bright sprite) and registers it on‑the‑fly, so the shield badge appears without any style changes.

> **When to use** – This is handy for a quick demo or when you truly cannot modify the style JSON. For production you’ll usually prefer option 1 or 2 because it avoids per‑frame JavaScript work and keeps the network requests predictable.

---

## TL;DR – Exact image names you need

```
us-interstate_1 … us-interstate_6
us-highway_1   … us-highway_6
us-state_1     … us-state_6
road_1         … road_6
```

Make sure those 22 IDs exist in **any** sprite sheet that the style loads (either the single `sprite` URL, or one of the entries in the `sprite` array). The easiest way is to point `sprite` at the official OpenMapTiles / OSM‑Bright sprite, or add a second sprite sheet that contains just those images and give it the `default` id.

Once the sprite with those IDs is available, the shield badges will render automatically—no layer edits required. Happy mapping!
